subject: Inflated beta estimates (and SE) with the addition of a colonization covariate -- colext()

messages.author: 0fc0d386d661ccc8
messages.subject: Inflated beta estimates (and SE) with the addition of a colonization covariate -- colext()
parts:
Good afternoon,

I am building dynamic occupancy models to understand factors that drive annual and seasonal shifts in red-headed woodpecker habitat use.  The model I am working on currently uses point count data collected during the summers of 2016 and 2017 (2 primary periods).  

I started with simple models and added covariates in a stepwise fashion, comparing AIC scores at each stage.  First, I added covariates for detection (p), then initial occupancy (psi), then colonization (gamma).  Eventually, I would fit covariates for the extinction parameter (epsilon), but I ran into trouble while fitting covariates for colonization (gamma):

# Colonization (gamma)
Fm0 <- colext(~PrOpen + st_dens + snags + burn, ~1, ~1, ~wind, data = umf)
Fm1 <- colext(~PrOpen + st_dens + snags + burn, ~st_dens, ~1, ~wind, data = umf)
Fm2 <- colext(~PrOpen + st_dens + snags + burn, ~mast, ~1, ~wind, data = umf)
Fm3 <- colext(~PrOpen + st_dens + snags + burn, ~pines, ~1, ~wind, data = umf)
Fm4 <- colext(~PrOpen + st_dens + snags + burn, ~snags, ~1, ~wind, data = umf)
Fm5 <- colext(~PrOpen + st_dens + snags + burn, ~W, ~1, ~wind, data = umf)
Fm6 <- colext(~PrOpen + st_dens + snags + burn, ~SDI, ~1, ~wind, data = umf)
Fm7 <- colext(~PrOpen + st_dens + snags + burn, ~PrOpen, ~1, ~wind, data = umf)
Fm8 <- colext(~PrOpen + st_dens + snags + burn, ~burn, ~1, ~wind, data = umf)
Fm9 <- colext(~PrOpen + st_dens + snags + burn, ~mast + bugs, ~1, ~wind, data = umf)

# Model comparison ***Code abbreviated here***
ms <- modSel(models)
ms

However, after fitting a few covariates, the beta and intercept estimates for colonization (gamma) get wacky and their SE are enormous:

Has anyone else run into similar issues?  Should I be concerned about the inflated betas and SE (I'm thinking yes)?  I tried specifying starting values from the simple model (starts = c(coef(Fm0), 0, 0)), but that did not help.  My covariates are all standardized.  When I ran models in a similar fashion for my winter point count data (2 primary winter sampling periods) I did not run into this problem.  I really appreciate any insight from the 'unmarked' community!

Ben Nickley
